name: Tourist Entry (Visa-Exempt E-Ticket) / Tourist Visa (TS/TM)

requirements.blocker_text: Most nationalities (US, Canada, UK, EU, Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Mexico, most South/Central American countries, Japan, Israel, and others) do not need a visa to enter as a tourist -- illustrative list, not exhaustive; the official site does not publish a single complete list.
All passengers on commercial flights must complete a free electronic entry/exit form (e-Ticket) at eticket.migracion.gob.do before or on arrival.
Passport must be valid for at least six months.
Round-trip airline, maritime, or land ticket is required, plus a permanent address in the Dominican Republic and proof of sufficient economic solvency.
Non-exempt nationals must apply at a Dominican consulate: visa form, 2x2 photo, proof of funds, return flight reservation, and hotel booking or invitation letter.
requirements.fix_path: Apply at the nearest Dominican consulate.

evidence_required.document: Completed e-Ticket (visa-exempt) or Tourist Visa TS/TM (non-exempt)

outcome.duration_length: 30 days standard tourist stay, extendable up to 120 days total via paid extension (RD$3,500-5,600); Tourist Visa TS/TM valid 60 days

sources.title: Ministerio de Turismo República Dominicana -- official entry requirements: visa-exempt nationalities, passport validity, return ticket, economic solvency, exit tax
Dirección General de Migración -- tourist stay extension (PRÓRROGA DE ESTADÍA PARA TURISTAS): 30-day standard stay, e-Ticket requirement, extension fees and duration up to 120 days
MIREX Portal Único de Servicios de Relaciones Exteriores -- Tourist Visa (TS/TM): 60-day duration, single/multiple entry, requirements

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Dominican Republic). The official Ministry of Tourism page gives an illustrative, not exhaustive, list of visa-exempt nationalities -- modeled the nationality check as hard:false since no single authoritative complete list was found at tier-1 precision. Standard tourist entry is 30 days; extensions are available up to 120 days total for a fee, confirmed directly on the DGM's own extension-service page. Non-exempt nationals go through a distinct Tourist Visa (TS/TM) process via MIREX consulates instead of the e-Ticket system -- modeled as a second OR-group. switchable_to reflects that DGM's own RT-9 page notes a reduced solvency threshold for those married to a Dominican, and that status changes in-country are a normal part of the DGM migratory-category-change process (see do_permanent_residence notes).
